observations.notes: Operates 3.0 MMTPA granulated urea complex in Lekki, Lagos; expanding to 9.0 MMTPA Nigeria + 3.0 MMTPA Ethiopia ($7bn expansion backed by $600m AFC facility approved mid-2026).

financials_multi_year.source: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) $600m Facility Announcement & Expansion Filings (Mid-26), read 26-Nov-26

observations.notes: Greenview Fertiliser Corp (Dangote Fertiliser holding arm) secured a $600m facility from AFC in mid-2026 toward a $7bn expansion program tripling Nigeria urea capacity toward 9 Mtpa plus Ethiopia development. Standalone audited P&L remains private.

recovery_analysis.thesis: Greenview Fertiliser / Dangote Fertiliser secured a $600m AFC facility in mid-2026 to back a $7bn expansion targeting 9 Mtpa capacity and Ethiopia development. Hard-currency urea exports insulate against naira weakness, though standalone audited P&L and parent DIL intercompany terms remain private. Structural recovery anchored by Nigeria materials asset perimeter and DANFER 7.75% 2031 ($750m) / 11.50% 2028 seniority.

annotations.note: Greenview Fertiliser secured $600m AFC facility for $7bn expansion to 9 Mtpa; standalone P&L private.
Issued $750m 7.75% 2031 Eurobond and secured $600m AFC facility in Jun 2026 for Nigeria urea expansion and Ethiopia plant.
Producer is positioned in the bottom quartile (Q1) of global production costs, preserving positive EBITDA generation across cyclical commodity troughs.
>75% of revenues billed in USD/EUR against predominantly local-currency operating expenditures, creating a structural natural FX hedge.
Controls world-class mineral or petrochemical reserves essential to the domestic economy, ensuring sovereign backstop support in stress scenarios.

verdict.stance: Neutral / Export-Oriented Hard-Currency Urea Producer (Private Filings)
verdict.summary: Greenview Fertiliser / Dangote Fertiliser secured a $600m AFC facility in mid-2026 to back a $7bn expansion targeting 9 Mtpa capacity and Ethiopia development. Hard-currency urea exports insulate against naira weakness, though standalone audited P&L and parent DIL intercompany terms remain private.

positives: First-quartile global urea cost position via captive Nigerian natural gas feedstock and Lekki Free Zone export terminal.
Secured $750m 7.75% 2031 Eurobond and $600m AFC facility (Jun-26), demonstrating deep international & DFI liquidity access.
USD-denominated export revenues insulate debt service from Naira depreciation.
negatives: Large multi-billion dollar expansion capex across Nigeria urea trains and Ethiopia fertilizer complex.
Capped by Nigerian sovereign ceiling ('B') and domestic gas supply/pipeline reliability risks.
Group-level capital allocation and related-party linkages across Dangote ecosystem.
